articles.title: Advanced function parameters in Python: defaults, *args, and **kwargs
articles.excerpt: The function you wrote in the previous tutorial had one or two parameters. The one you'll write in six months will have eight. Someone on the team added four without telling anyone, one has a name nob…
articles.body: The function you wrote in the previous tutorial had one or two parameters. The one you'll write in six months will have eight. Someone on the team added four without telling anyone, one has a name nobody remembers the origin of, the seventh is a boolean called flag whose behavior depends on the value of the parameter before it, and there's a mode that "makes sense in context." This isn't a prediction; it's just how software grows. Python has tools to keep this from becoming a disaster: default parameters, keyword arguments, *args , and **kwargs . This lesson covers all of them — including why one of them has a trap that's caught more programmers than will admit it.
articles.author: Javi Palacios

articles.title: C++ Static Variables, Static Members Explained: One Class, Many Objects, One Shared Counter
articles.excerpt: Before Classes: What Does static Actually Mean in C++? Before we discuss static members inside a class, let's understand static without involving classes at all. Imagine you're building a system that…
articles.body: Before Classes: What Does static Actually Mean in C++? Before we discuss static members inside a class, let's understand static without involving classes at all. Imagine you're building a system that tracks how many times a function has been called. Every time the function runs, you want to increase a counter. Sounds simple, right? But there's a problem. A Normal Local Variable: Created, Used, Destroyed Consider this function: `#include using namespace std; void processRequest() { int count = 0; count++; cout << count << '\n'; } int main() { processRequest(); processRequest(); processRequest(); }` Output: 1 1 1 Why doesn't the output reach 3? Every time processRequest() is called: A new local variable count is initialized to 0. count++ increments it to 1.

articles.title: My OpenAPI diff missed a renamed path because JSON Schema doesn't see strings
articles.excerpt: I spent a morning debugging why my changelog generator reported zero breaking changes between two API specs that had obviously moved an entire endpoint. Turned out the specs were fine — my diff was co…
articles.body: I spent a morning debugging why my changelog generator reported zero breaking changes between two API specs that had obviously moved an entire endpoint. Turned out the specs were fine — my diff was comparing the wrong thing. The bug: I was hashing the path strings themselves to detect renames. /v1/users/{id} renamed to /v2/accounts/{id} looks like delete-plus-add, not a move, so it surfaced as two changes instead of one rename with a version bump. Worse, if the old path was also deleted in the same release, my diff logic sometimes matched the wrong pairs and reported a "rename" that never happened. The fix wasn't clever string similarity — it was structural.

articles.title: Contract notice period reminders: how to catch the window before an auto-renewal
articles.excerpt: This article is AI-generated. Many service, software, equipment and maintenance contracts renew automatically unless you give notice. The trap isn't the renewal date itself. It's the notice period in…
articles.body: This article is AI-generated. Many service, software, equipment and maintenance contracts renew automatically unless you give notice. The trap isn't the renewal date itself. It's the notice period in front of it. If a contract ends on 31 January and requires 90 days' written notice, the real deadline is early November, and by the time anyone notices the end date, the decision has already been made for you. This guide shows a simple routine that works in any spreadsheet: a register that records the notice deadline rather than just the end date, one formula that tells you which contracts need a decision now, a fixed sequence for deciding and sending notice, and a habit of writing down proof that notice went out.

articles.body: If you've been building applications with C#, you've probably experienced this at least once. Your API runs perfectly on your laptop. Your database connection works. articles.title: A faint glow from the early universe could help solve the mystery of dark energy
articles.excerpt: Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy.
articles.body: Hydrogen may be the most common element in the cosmos, but scientists could use it to do something unique: uncover the nature of dark energy, the mysterious force driving the accelerating expansion of the universe. This new line of dark energy investigation comes from the fact that researchers have determined that the CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) project can detect the faint radio glow of hydrogen from the universe's distant past. Not only does this represent a faster and much less expensive way to investigate dark energy, but it is a major milestone for CHIME. The instrument was specifically devised to investigate dark energy and its pervasive influence.

Then there’s the Groundhog Day -like season 6 episode “Monday,” which sees Agent Mulder (David Duchovny) and Agent Scully (Gillian Anderson) repeatedly trying to stop a bank bombing while experiencing the same day over and over again. articles.body: SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. articles.body: Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies. The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster . The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.
